hints: Focus on how an addition polymer forms, each C=C double bond in a monomer opens up to become a C-C single bond pair in the chain.
Split the long carbon backbone into two-carbon pairs, notice one pair type is C(Cl)(CH3)-C(H)(Cl) and the other is C(Cl)(CH3)-C(H)(CH3).
Put the double bond back between each pair to rebuild the alkenes, then count the longest carbon chain and Cl positions to name them.
walkthrough:
**Recall how addition polymers unzip**

Think backwards. In addition polymerisation, each monomer alkene $C=C$ becomes a $-C-C-$ unit in the polymer.

To find the monomers, cut the backbone into 2-carbon sections and restore the $C=C$ double bond.

**Spot the two different repeat pairs**

Look carefully along the chain. It alternates between two distinct 2-carbon units.

Unit 1: $-C(Cl)(CH_3)-C(H)(Cl)-$
$$-C(Cl)(CH_3)-C(H)(Cl)- \rightarrow C(Cl)(CH_3)=C(H)(Cl)$$
Unit 2: $-C(Cl)(CH_3)-C(H)(CH_3)-$
$$-C(Cl)(CH_3)-C(H)(CH_3)- \rightarrow C(Cl)(CH_3)=C(H)(CH_3)$$

**Name each rebuilt alkene**

For Unit 1, the $C=C$ has 3 carbons in total including the $CH_3$ branch, so it is a propene with two Cl atoms. That is 1,2-dichloropropene, $CH_3-CCl=C(H)Cl$.

For Unit 2, the $C=C$ has 4 carbons in total including two $CH_3$ groups, so it is a butene with one Cl. That is 2-chlorobut-2-ene, $CH_3-CCl=C(H)CH_3$.

**Match to the options**

The pair needed is 1,2-dichloropropene and 2-chlorobut-2-ene. This is a copolymer made from two different monomers alternating along the chain.

options.A: Correct. The $C(Cl)(CH_3)=C(H)(Cl)$ unit is a 3-carbon propene with Cl on C1 and C2, and the $C(Cl)(CH_3)=C(H)(CH_3)$ unit is a 4-carbon but-2-ene with Cl on C2. Together they give exactly the alternating pattern seen.
options.B: Incorrect. 2,3-dichlorobut-2-ene would be $CH_3-CCl=CCl-CH_3$ with Cl on both C atoms of the double bond, but neither unit in the polymer has that pattern. Chloropropene would have only one Cl, but one of the units clearly has two Cl atoms.
options.C: Incorrect. Chloroethene is $CH_2=CHCl$ with only 2 carbons and no $CH_3$ branch. Every 2-carbon unit in this polymer carries at least one $CH_3$ group, so a 2-carbon monomer cannot fit.
options.D: Incorrect. 2-chlorobut-2-ene is right for one unit, but chloropropene has only one Cl. The other unit in the polymer is $-C(Cl)(CH_3)-C(H)(Cl)-$ which has two Cl atoms, so it must be a dichloropropene, not a monochloropropene.
